title: arXiv Trending Physics — Daily (2026-10-23 batch)
global_caveat: This is an inferred notable-paper ranking, not an official arXiv trending chart. arXiv publishes no official readership/trending ranking, and citation evidence is sparse for papers this new.
ranking_context: Semantic Scholar Graph API current citation totals for the selected papers were zero at the snapshot, so citation momentum did not separate same-day submissions; ordering relies on expert attention and checkable result, cross-listing, publication, and data-release signals.

sections.title: Natural Chlorine Enhances Antineutrino Detection in the Deep Ocean
sections.authors: Ruike Cao, Iwan Morton-Blake, Donglian Xu, Qichao Chang, Shuhua Hao et al.
sections.abstract: The authors propose using naturally abundant seawater chlorine to tag inverse-beta-decay antineutrinos through a brighter, faster neutron-capture cascade, combining a detector simulation with a salted-water laboratory test.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report correlated neutron-capture signatures in a salted-water test and estimate that chlorine tagging could extend TRIDENT's simulated core-collapse-supernova 5σ reach from about 50 kpc to over 100 kpc.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; a China Jinping Underground Laboratory salted-water test, plus detector-level TRIDENT simulation.
sections.unique_caveat: In the salt-plus-background test the neutron-capture excess is about 2σ; the >100 kpc reach is simulated, and time-variable bioluminescence is not included in that sensitivity estimate.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Included in neutrino physicist Mauricio Bustamante's daily arXiv picks; it pairs a detector-level simulation with a separate salted-water demonstration, giving it both an independent attention signal and a concrete experimental basis.

sections.title: Observation of Polarization Topology in Magneto-Optical BICs
sections.authors: Yaqi Li, Mingyu Tong, Fujia Chen, Li Zhang, Rui Zhao et al.
sections.abstract: The authors reconstruct the far-field polarization texture of a magneto-optical bound state in the continuum, finding a +1 topological charge whose surrounding handedness can be reversed by magnetic-bias tuning.
sections.claimed_result: Using polarization-resolved angle-dependent reflection and singular-value decomposition, the authors measure a 2π winding (charge +1) and show opposite polarization handedness at two magnetic-bias strengths.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; a fabricated magneto-optical photonic-crystal slab, reflection-matrix measurements, and a coupled-mode interpretation.
sections.unique_caveat: The apparatus cannot measure the central angular region (|θ| < 6°), so the topological charge is reconstructed from the surrounding accessible texture; the demonstration is on one device design.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A direct experimental resolution of a previously difficult nonreciprocal polarization texture, with a distinctive controlled reversal of handedness while the measured charge remains fixed.

sections.title: Measurements of the branching fractions of Λc+→ΛK+π0 and Λc+→ΛK+η decays at Belle and Belle II
sections.authors: M. Abumusabh, I. Adachi, A. Aggarwal, Y. Ahn, H. Aihara et al. (Belle and Belle II Collaborations)
sections.abstract: Using combined Belle and Belle II data, the collaborations measure two singly Cabibbo-suppressed charmed-baryon decays and report the first observation of Λc+→ΛK+η.
sections.claimed_result: The authors measure B(Λc+→ΛK+η)/B(Λc+→Λπ+π0)=(8.73±0.35±0.43)×10−3 and observe the η mode above 10σ; its rate is larger than the cited SU(3)-flavor-symmetry predictions.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; Belle and Belle II e+e− collision data (980 fb−1 and 570 fb−1, respectively).
sections.unique_caveat: Absolute branching fractions inherit the uncertainty in the world-average reference decay; the authors also note that three-body decay dynamics and possible intermediate resonances complicate interpretation of the theory discrepancy.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The first observation of a decay mode at greater than 10σ, using 1.55 ab−1 combined across two detector datasets; the related ΛK+π0 result substantially improves the prior precision.

sections.title: A cosmic filament catalog for COSMOS-Web Data Release 1 across 0.5 < z < 3.5
sections.authors: Qiaoyang Hao, Tao Wang, Weishan Zhu, Hong Guo, Peng Wang et al.
sections.abstract: The authors combine photometric-redshift probability distributions with simulation-calibrated filament extraction to release a COSMOS-Web cosmic-web catalog spanning redshift 0.5–3.5.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a catalog of 12,523 filaments across 0.5<z<3.5 built from COSMOS-Web DR1 and calibrated against TNG simulations, with mock tests indicating improved recovery over a single-redshift-slice baseline.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; COSMOS-Web DR1, with TNG simulation light-cone mocks used for calibration and validation.
sections.unique_caveat: The 2D extraction depends on photometric-redshift PDFs and simulation-driven thresholds; Gaussian PDF approximations, projection effects, and method choice can change completeness and purity.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A reusable release of 12,523 filaments, 136,210 segments, and probability maps, cross-listed across cosmology, galaxies, and methods; the paper is published in Astronomy & Astrophysics (DOI 10.1051/0004-6361/202659407).

sections.title: QUIJOTE scientific results - XII. Characterization of the polarized synchrotron emission at the power spectrum level in the QUIJOTE-MFI wide survey
sections.authors: F. Vansyngel, J. A. Rubino-Martin, P. de Ferra, R. B. Barreiro, R. T. Genova-Santos et al.
sections.abstract: The authors combine QUIJOTE-MFI, Planck, and WMAP polarization maps to measure Galactic synchrotron power spectra and estimate their impact on future CMB B-mode searches.
sections.claimed_result: For multipoles 30<ℓ<130, the authors find a possible BB-versus-EE synchrotron steepening at only about 1.6σ and estimate equivalent synchrotron power of r≈0.003 at 90 GHz and r≈0.0002 at 150 GHz.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; QUIJOTE-MFI wide survey (10–20 GHz) combined with Planck and WMAP.
sections.unique_caveat: The apparent BB/EE slope difference is not statistically strong (about 1.6σ), and the foreground estimates apply to the analyzed multipole range and sky masks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted for MNRAS and combines three microwave datasets to provide quantitative foreground estimates directly relevant to primordial B-mode measurements.

sections.title: Experimental evidence of forward energy transfer induced by core-edge coupling in multiscale tokamak turbulence
sections.authors: F. Chen, Z. M. Shen, N. Sun, P. Li, Z. Y. Qiu et al.
sections.abstract: Combining two plasma-scattering diagnostics, the authors report evidence that an edge-originating quasi-coherent mode couples to core turbulence and transfers energy toward smaller scales.
sections.claimed_result: The authors interpret the observed core-edge coupling and secondary instabilities as evidence for net forward energy transfer from ion to electron scales in the measured tokamak turbulence.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; multichannel collective Thomson scattering and radially localized Doppler backscattering.
sections.unique_caveat: This is evidence from a tokamak measurement, not confirmation that the same cascade operates across machines or plasma regimes; broader replication is needed before generalizing the interpretation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A direct experimental result on a core-scale process relevant to fusion transport, supported by complementary collective Thomson-scattering and Doppler-backscattering measurements.

sections.title: A Robust Estimator for the Lyman-α Forest 1D Power Spectrum at High Redshift
sections.authors: Molly Wolfson, Joseph F. Hennawi, Frederick B. Davies, Zarija Lukić
sections.abstract: The authors validate a likelihood-based estimator designed to recover the high-redshift Lyα flux power spectrum despite limited spectra, instrumental effects, noise, and missing pixels.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that pixel-covariance maximum-likelihood inference recovers mock input power spectra within expected errors across tested scales under the modeled resolution, sampling, noise, and missing-data effects.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; analytic Gaussian mocks and forward-modeled high-redshift quasar-spectrum simulations.
sections.unique_caveat: Validation is on mocks rather than a new measurement from observed high-redshift spectra; robustness is only demonstrated for the observational effects included in those simulations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across cosmology and galaxy astrophysics; the method is tested against known-input realizations and forward-modeled observational complications at z≥5.

sections.title: Gravitational Wave Diffractive Images Reveal the Structure of Astrophysical Objects
sections.authors: Han Gil Choi, Sunghoon Jung, Volodymyr Takhistov
sections.abstract: The authors derive how gravitational-wave diffraction can encode a lens's projected mass profile and forecast whether next-generation detectors could distinguish extended dark matter structures from point lenses.
sections.claimed_result: The authors forecast that five years of next-generation observations could distinguish extended lenses from point masses down to dark-matter fractions of order 10−5, and halo-dressed primordial black holes down to order 10−6, for their assumed source populations.
sections.evidence_type: Forecast/proposal; analytic lensing relations and numerical wave-optics calculations for assumed source and lens populations.
sections.unique_caveat: These are forecasts, not detections; the reach depends on the assumed source population, source-lens geometry, lens models, and future detector sensitivities.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A cross-listed theoretical framework spanning four physics archives, backed by full numerical wave-optics calculations and explicit sensitivity forecasts for dark-matter structures and black-hole environments.
